boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Appalachian State University
boards.description: When the library closes or the mountain air gets cold, these late-night spots provide the fuel for Appalachian State students to keep going through the night in Boone.

cards.title: The King Street Tray Run
cards.subtitle: 664 West King Street, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Order a Cook Out Tray with a milkshake at this downtown staple. It is a primary late-night destination for students, often open until 3:00 AM or later on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A high-volume fast-food landmark famous for its customizable trays and 40+ milkshake flavors, located walking distance from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out on West King Street is open until 3:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 4:00 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru and walk-up window available late; hours extend to 4:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: 24-Hour Hashbrown Retreat
cards.subtitle: 881 Blowing Rock Road, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Head here for scattered, smothered, and covered hashbrowns at any hour. It is the reliable 24/7 fallback for late-night study breaks or post-event meals.
cards.short_summary: A classic 24-hour diner located just south of campus, serving breakfast favorites and comfort food around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House #2031 at 881 Blowing Rock Road is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: The Midnight Cookie Delivery
cards.subtitle: 128 Appalachian Street, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Satisfy a late-night sweet tooth with warm cookies delivered directly to dorms or available for pickup downtown until 3:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in warm cookie delivery and late-night treats, popular for late-night study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies in Boone is open and delivers until 3:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Open for walk-in and delivery until 3:00 AM.

cards.title: Central Dining Hall Late Hours
cards.subtitle: 480 Rivers Street, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Utilize your meal plan for a late dinner at the university's main dining hall, which serves as a central hub for student life until 10:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-access dining facility on campus, offering various food stations and late-evening dining for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Street Café (Central Dining Hall) is open until 10:30 PM daily during the regular academic year.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours - App State Campus Dining
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:30 PM; accepts meal plan swipes and dining dollars.

cards.title: Trivette Hall Evening Fuel
cards.subtitle: 190 Trivette Hall Drive, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Visit the west campus dining hub for a late-night meal by the pond. It serves the residential community on the west side of campus until 10:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: An all-access dining hall located in Trivette Hall, providing late-evening food options for students on the west side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Place at the Pond in Trivette Hall is open until 10:30 PM daily.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours - App State Campus Dining
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:30 PM; accepts meal plan swipes.

cards.title: The Late-Night Sandwich Spot
cards.subtitle: 455 Blowing Rock Road, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Grab a 'dank' sandwich or potato wedges at this inclusive local favorite. It stays open until 2:00 AM every night, serving a full menu late.
cards.short_summary: A popular local eatery and bar known for its creative sandwiches, vegan options, and late-night kitchen hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Lily's Snack Bar is open daily from 3:00 PM to 2:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Kitchen serves full menu until 2:00 AM; under-21 safe for dining.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Golden Arches
cards.subtitle: 896 Blowing Rock Road, Boone, NC
cards.notes: A reliable 24-hour drive-thru option for a quick burger or fries when everything else is closed. It is located just a short drive from campus.
cards.short_summary: A standard 24-hour fast-food location providing consistent late-night service to the Boone community.
cards.evidence_claim: The McDonald's at 896 Blowing Rock Road is open 24 hours daily.
cards.source_title: McDonald's - 896 Blowing Rock Rd, Boone, NC
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is open 24/7.

cards.title: Late-Night Fourth Meal
cards.subtitle: 1093 Blowing Rock Road, Boone, NC
cards.notes: The go-to for late-night tacos and burritos. The drive-thru typically serves students and locals until 1:00 AM or 2:00 AM on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food chain location offering Mexican-inspired fare with late-night drive-thru hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell at 1093 Blowing Rock Road is open until 1:00 AM or later for drive-thru service.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open late; check app for exact nightly closing times.

cards.title: Late-Night Road Food
cards.subtitle: 1711 Highway 105, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Enjoy high-quality burgers and wild game options until midnight on weekends. It offers a more elevated late-night dining experience in a casual setting.
cards.short_summary: A local restaurant serving 'classic American road food' with a focus on fresh, house-prepared ingredients and late-night hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cardinal is open until midnight Thursday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Kitchen open until midnight on weekends; all ages welcome for dining.

cards.title: The Late-Night Frosty Run
cards.subtitle: 1016 Blowing Rock Road, Boone, NC
cards.notes: Stop by for a late-night Frosty or a burger. The drive-thru remains open until midnight or later, providing another quick option on the main thoroughfare.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food restaurant known for square burgers and Frosty desserts, offering late-night drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's at 1016 Blowing Rock Road is open late, with drive-thru hours typically extending to midnight or 1:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open late; lobby hours may vary.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student spaces at App State, from quiet sensory rooms and rooftop patios to collaborative business commons and riverside parks.

cards.title: Belk Library Sensory Room
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Belk Library & Information Commons
cards.notes: Use this private first-floor room for sensory regulation; it features floor rockers, white noise machines, and low lighting for 45-minute sessions.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated private space on the first floor of Belk Library designed for sensory regulation and stress relief.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sensory Room is a first-come, first-served private room on the 1st floor of Belk Library with floor rockers, cushions, and white noise machines.
cards.source_title: Sensory Room - Appalachian State University Library
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff on a first-come, first-served basis; users are asked to limit sessions to 45 minutes.

cards.title: Summit Trail Solarium
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Study among indoor plants and water features in this glass-walled space; visit the second-floor balcony for a quieter view of the greenery.
cards.short_summary: A large, plant-filled indoor garden space within the student union used for studying and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Summit Trail Solarium is a student union space filled with chairs, plants, and water features, accessible on the first floor with a balcony on the second.
cards.source_title: Building Maps | Plemmons Student Union - Appalachian State University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Plemmons Student Union operating hours; typically open late during the academic semester.

cards.title: Howard's Knob Rooftop Patio
cards.subtitle: Third Floor, Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for this outdoor terrace featuring tables with umbrellas and views of the surrounding mountains.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor rooftop terrace on the third floor of the student union providing mountain views and study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard's Knob Patio is an outside space on the 3rd floor of the student union with views and 25 tables with umbrellas.
cards.source_title: Howard's Knob Patio | Conference and Event Services | Appalachian State University
cards.access_notes: Open for general student use when not reserved for private events; accessible via the third floor of the PSU.

cards.title: Durham Park
cards.subtitle: Rivers Street and University Drive
cards.notes: Find a quieter outdoor alternative to Sanford Mall along Boone Creek; look for the weeping willow tree and gazebo for a shaded study spot.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil campus park featuring a creek, gazebo, and walking paths, often less crowded than central quads.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham Park is located off Blowing Rock Road between University Drive and Rivers Street and includes a portion of Boone Creek and a gazebo.
cards.source_title: OPINION: Beauty in simplicity: App State's underrated park - The Appalachian
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible park managed by the university; always open for walking and lounging.

cards.title: Broyhill Commons
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Peacock Hall
cards.notes: Visit the 'Living Room' of the Walker College of Business for collaborative group work and networking near the student-run coffee shop.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative networking and study lounge located on the second floor of Peacock Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Broyhill Commons is a large open area on the second floor of Peacock Hall that serves as a networking space for students.
cards.source_title: 2015: The Broyhill Commons opens in Peacock Hall, fosters collaboration
cards.access_notes: Open during Peacock Hall building hours; accessible to all students for networking and study.

cards.title: Erneston Music Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Broyhill Music Center
cards.notes: Reserve one of four study rooms in this specialized library; note that only water in sealed containers is permitted inside.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study rooms located within the music library, ideal for students seeking a focused environment away from the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Erneston Music Library on the 2nd floor of Broyhill Music Center has four study rooms available for student use.
cards.access_notes: Rooms are available only while the Music Library is open; reservations are recommended.

cards.title: Rich Mountain Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Third Floor, Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Find this quiet retreat on the third floor for personal reflection or meditation; it is located near the rooftop patio.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet space in the student union for meditation and silent reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rich Mountain Meditation Room (Room 302) is located on the third floor of the Plemmons Student Union.
cards.source_title: Building Maps | Plemmons Student Union - Appalachian State University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during student union hours; intended for quiet use only.

cards.entity_name: Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.subtitle: 423 West King Street
cards.notes: Explore six galleries of contemporary art for free; ask a student gallery ambassador for insights into current exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: The university's visual arts center featuring multiple galleries with rotating contemporary exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Turchin Center is always free and it features six galleries with changing exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Visit | Turchin Center for the Visual Arts | Appalachian State University
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Thursday and Saturday 10am-6pm, Friday 12pm-8pm; closed Sundays, Mondays, and during home football games.

cards.entity_name: Reich College of Education Media Lab
cards.title: Reich College of Education Media Lab
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Reich College of Education
cards.notes: Access Mac and PC labs or professional recording studios; students enrolled in education courses can also check out digital media equipment.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused space providing digital media tools and recording studios for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Media Lab on the 1st floor of the RCOE building provides Mac and PC labs and professional recording studios.
cards.source_title: Digital Learning Resources and Media Lab | Reich College of Education
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.; equipment checkout requires enrollment in an RCOE course.

cards.title: Wiseman's View Lounge
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Relax in this second-floor lounge area located near the vending machines and the Solarium balcony.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable student lounge area located on the second floor of the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Wiseman's View Lounge (Room 224) is located on the second floor of the Plemmons Student Union near the vending area.
cards.source_title: Building Maps | Plemmons Student Union - Appalachian State University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during student union operating hours for general student use.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best spots around Appalachian State University for social activities and relaxation that require no admission or purchase, from campus landmarks to scenic mountain overlooks.

cards.entity_name: Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Browse Contemporary Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: King Street Art Hub
cards.notes: Explore six galleries of contemporary art with rotating exhibitions. Admission is always free for students and the public; check for Friday evening exhibition celebrations.
cards.short_summary: A university-run visual arts center featuring local and international contemporary works with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the center is always free. The Turchin Center for the Visual Arts in Boone, North Carolina welcomes visitors to experience the arts... Admission is always FREE.
cards.source_title: Visit | Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Thursday and Saturday 10am-6pm, Friday 12pm-8pm. Closed Sundays, Mondays, and during home football games.

cards.title: Hammock and Socialize on the Quad
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Join the campus community on this central green space for hammocking, slacklining, or people-watching. It is the primary hub for student-led events and outdoor lounging.
cards.short_summary: The central grassy quad of App State, serving as the main social gathering point for outdoor activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanford Mall is the name of a green area of campus that hosts all sorts of outdoor booths... It is also where students meet to practice rope walking or to swing or just hang out.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space available 24/7; most active during daylight hours between classes.

cards.title: Study in the 24-Hour Commons
cards.subtitle: Late Night Study Hub
cards.notes: Utilize five floors of study space, including quiet zones and group rooms. Students have 24/5 access with an AppCard; community members are welcome during daylight hours.
cards.short_summary: The main university library offering extensive study spaces, technology resources, and 24-hour access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Belk Library and Information Commons... Open 24 hours a day, Sunday - Thursday... After midnight, Belk Library is only open to students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours Sunday-Thursday for students. Public access ends at midnight. AppCard required for late-night entry.

cards.title: Paint the Expression Tunnels
cards.subtitle: Under Rivers Street
cards.notes: Grab a can of spray paint and add your own art to the walls of the tunnels connecting campus. This is the only designated area where graffiti is officially encouraged.
cards.short_summary: Pedestrian tunnels under Rivers Street where students are permitted to use spray paint for creative expression and announcements.
cards.evidence_claim: The expression tunnels under Rivers Street are the only place at Appalachian State where graffiti and other forms of art and vandalism are not only allowed, but encouraged.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 via pedestrian paths under Rivers Street near Rankin Science Hall.

cards.title: Visit the Unofficial Mascots
cards.subtitle: Campus Wildlife Retreat
cards.notes: Relax by the water and watch the resident ducks, often called the university's unofficial mascots. It's a peaceful spot for a quick break between classes on the west side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus pond and park area home to a variety of domesticated ducks and a popular spot for student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The ducks at Appalachian State University have been referred to as “the best unofficial mascots in college” and provide joy to everyone who visits them at the Duck Pond.
cards.access_notes: Public park area accessible 24/7. Located near the Rivers Street Parking Deck.

cards.title: Picnic by Boone Creek
cards.subtitle: Secluded Campus Green
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot in this often-overlooked park featuring a gazebo and the flowing Boone Creek. Ideal for a peaceful picnic or reading away from the busier Sanford Mall.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil, wooded park on campus featuring a creek, walking paths, and a gazebo.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham Park is located off Blowing Rock Road... It includes a portion of Boone Creek... the park offers a calm space for whatever one may need it for.
cards.source_title: OPINION: Beauty in simplicity: App State's underrated park
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; located between University Drive and Rivers Street.

cards.title: Relax in the Indoor Garden
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Warm up during winter in this glass-enclosed space featuring tropical plants and water fountains. It's a favorite indoor hang for students looking for natural light and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A sun-filled indoor garden and lounge area within the student union, perfect for year-round relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The addition, known as the Summit Trail Solarium, features a passive-solar, south-facing garden environment, ambient water fountains, and sky-lit reading areas.
cards.source_title: Appalachian State University – Plemmons Student Union Solarium
cards.access_notes: Open during Plemmons Student Union hours: Mon-Fri 7am-11pm, Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 3pm-11pm.

cards.title: View Boone from the Skybridge
cards.subtitle: Panoramic Mountain Overlook
cards.notes: Walk the new ADA-accessible skybridge for a 1,000-foot-high view of the campus and town. It's a short drive or steep hike from downtown and offers free admission.
cards.short_summary: A county park overlooking Boone featuring a newly renovated accessible skybridge with panoramic mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The centerpiece of the project is a new ADA-accessible skybridge overlook... Admission is free.
cards.source_title: Howard Knob County Park Reopens With New $2.2 Million Skybridge Overlook
cards.access_notes: Open May 1 - October 20, 8:30 am to 7:30 pm. Free admission.

cards.title: Walk the New River Greenway
cards.subtitle: Accessible Nature Path
cards.notes: Walk, run, or bike along this paved trail following the South Fork of the New River. It connects campus to local parks and features historic ruins and picnic shelters.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use paved trail system through Boone offering scenic river views and easy access to nature.
cards.evidence_claim: This fully accessible trail is either paved or gravel... It follows and crosses the South Fork of the New River through open meadows and colorful forests.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk. Multiple trailheads available, including near State Farm Road.

cards.entity_name: Don Kennedy Trails at State Farm
cards.title: Run the Cross Country Trails
cards.subtitle: State Farm Fields
cards.notes: Train on the same four-mile trail system used by the university's cross country teams. These grass and dirt paths offer a soft surface for running along the river.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated cross country trail system at the State Farm Fields complex used for both team training and public recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Don Kennedy trails offer more than four miles of trails and courses sitting along the New River... home to the Appalachian men and women's cross country teams.
cards.source_title: Don Kennedy Trails at State Farm - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for running and walking when not in use for university athletic events.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From sun-drenched solariums to silent library floors, these ten campus environments offer the best physical setups for focused academic work at App State.

cards.title: The Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: Quiet Study Floor
cards.notes: Utilize the walled study carrels and cubicles with privacy screens for deep focus. This floor is strictly designated for silent, individual study.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent floor in Belk Library featuring privacy-screened cubicles and individual study carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of Belk Library is a designated quiet floor featuring walled study carrels and cubicles with privacy screens for individual study.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 during weekdays for students with AppCard; weekend hours vary.

cards.title: The Indoor Garden
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Study beside ambient water fountains and tropical plants in this passive-solar space. It offers a bright, warm refuge during cold mountain winters.
cards.short_summary: A sun-lit garden environment inside the student union featuring water features and sky-lit reading areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Summit Trail Solarium features a passive-solar garden environment with ambient water fountains and sky-lit reading areas.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during student union operating hours; typically 7am-11pm.

cards.title: The Archives Alcove
cards.subtitle: Belk Library 4th Floor
cards.notes: Work at large study tables surrounded by natural light and regional history. This space is ideal for quiet research and focused writing sessions.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, naturally lit reading room on the library's top floor housing rare books and university archives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Special Collections Research Center on the 4th floor has study tables and abundant natural light for researchers and students.
cards.source_title: Special Collections Reading Room - Appalachian State University Library
cards.access_notes: Hours are more limited than the main library; typically open 10am-4pm on weekdays.

cards.title: The Business Hub
cards.subtitle: Peacock Hall 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Grab a coffee from the student-run Beans 2 Brew and find a spot in this collaborative 'living room' designed for networking and group work.
cards.short_summary: A modern collaborative space in the Walker College of Business featuring flexible seating and a student-run coffee shop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Broyhill Commons is a large open area on the second floor of Peacock Hall that serves as a networking and study space for students.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; construction on Peacock Hall expansion may affect some adjacent areas through 2027.

cards.title: The Wellness District Living Room
cards.subtitle: Levine Hall 1st Floor
cards.notes: Spread out in the sunny two-story atrium. It features numerous comfortable study chairs and easy access to the Rise Market + Bakery.
cards.short_summary: A bright, multi-story atrium in the health sciences building with ample lounge seating and an on-site cafe.
cards.evidence_claim: The Leon Levine Hall of Health Sciences features a sunny two-story atrium that serves as a 'living room' for students to gather and study.
cards.source_title: Leon Levine Hall of Health Sciences Self-Guided Tour
cards.access_notes: Located off-main campus on State Farm Road; accessible via AppalCART bus service.

cards.title: The Melodic Retreat
cards.subtitle: Broyhill Music Center 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Find a quiet table among the scores and recordings. This specialized library offers a smaller, more intimate environment than Belk Library.
cards.short_summary: A specialized academic library for music students offering quiet study tables and group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nicholas Erneston Music Library is located on the second floor of the Broyhill Music Center and contains four study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; check library website for specific daily operating hours.

cards.title: The Rooftop Terrace
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Study outdoors at one of the 25 tables with umbrellas. This rooftop space offers fresh air and elevated views of the campus core.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor rooftop patio on the third floor of the student union with umbrella-shaded tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard's Knob Patio is an outdoor space on the 3rd floor of the student union with 25 tables, four chairs each, and umbrellas.
cards.source_title: Howard's Knob Patio | Conference and Event Services
cards.access_notes: Weather dependent; accessible during student union hours when not reserved for events.

cards.title: The Balcony Perch
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Choose this lounge for comfortable seating that overlooks the Solarium. It provides a slightly more elevated and quiet perspective on the union's hub.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor lounge in the student union offering comfortable seating and views of the Solarium below.
cards.evidence_claim: Wiseman's View Lounge is located on the second floor of the Plemmons Student Union near the Solarium Balcony.
cards.access_notes: Open during student union hours; no reservation required for general lounge use.

cards.title: The Tech-Ready Suite
cards.subtitle: Sanford Hall
cards.notes: Utilize one of the four active learning rooms equipped with smart stations and individual screens. Ideal for group projects requiring digital collaboration.
cards.short_summary: Modern classrooms in Sanford Hall with smart stations and data ports, available for student use when not in class.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanford Hall contains 4 Active Learning rooms with 4 smart stations, each with its own screen and data ports.
cards.access_notes: Available for student use when classes are not in session; check building schedules posted near doors.

cards.title: The Top-Floor Hideaway
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union 4th Floor
cards.notes: Head to the highest floor of the student union for a quieter lounge experience. This space is often less trafficked than the lower-level common areas.
cards.short_summary: A quiet lounge located on the fourth floor of the student union, offering a more secluded study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mountains-to-Sea Lounge is located on the fourth floor of the Plemmons Student Union.
cards.access_notes: Open during student union hours; accessible via the main elevators or grand staircase.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Appalachian State University, from the historic storefronts of King Street to the student housing hubs along Blowing Rock Road.

cards.title: Downtown's Main Thoroughfare
cards.subtitle: King Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic stretch to visit the Appalachian Theatre or browse local shops like High Country Souvenirs and Appalachian Sportswear.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial and cultural artery of downtown Boone, directly bordering the university's northern edge.
cards.evidence_claim: West King Street is home to the historic Appalachian Theatre and numerous university-affiliated retail shops like Appalachian Sportswear.
cards.access_notes: Public street with metered parking and wide sidewalks for pedestrians.

cards.title: The Student Pedestrian Hub
cards.subtitle: Howard Street Corridor
cards.notes: Navigate this narrow street to find student-focused housing complexes and the central Appalcart transit circle.
cards.short_summary: A secondary downtown street known for its high density of student housing and its role as a transit hub for the Appalcart system.
cards.evidence_claim: Howard Street serves as a major gateway for students and features the Appalcart Circle for public transportation.
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian-friendly street with frequent bus service via Appalcart.

cards.title: The Commercial Gateway
cards.subtitle: US-321 Corridor
cards.notes: Access major retail centers and large-scale student housing developments like The Standard at Boone along this busy route.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial corridor southeast of campus providing access to groceries, dining, and modern apartment complexes.
cards.evidence_claim: Blowing Rock Road is a primary gateway for shopping and home to large student housing projects like The Standard.
cards.access_notes: High-traffic vehicular corridor with sidewalks connecting to the university's south side.

cards.title: Historic Arts District
cards.subtitle: Depot Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Turchin Center for the Visual Arts or explore local outdoor outfitters like Footsloggers.
cards.short_summary: A historic street connecting King Street to the university's arts district, featuring galleries and local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: Depot Street is home to the Turchin Center for the Visual Arts and long-standing local businesses like Footsloggers.
cards.source_title: Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Public street with sidewalk access to university galleries and downtown shops.

cards.title: The Campus Spine
cards.subtitle: Rivers Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past the Holmes Convocation Center and Durham Park on this central road that bisects the campus.
cards.short_summary: The main internal thoroughfare of the Appalachian State campus, lined with academic buildings and athletic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Street is the location of the Holmes Convocation Center and Durham Park, serving as a primary campus artery.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible street with heavy pedestrian traffic and university bus stops.

cards.title: The Eastern Edge
cards.subtitle: Hardin Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find student-friendly townhomes and quick-service dining options just steps from the university's main entrance.
cards.short_summary: A busy street on the eastern edge of campus featuring a mix of student housing and commercial services.
cards.evidence_claim: Hardin Street features student housing like Steeplechase Hardin Street and is located across from the main university entrance.
cards.access_notes: Public street with sidewalks; primarily used for access to east campus and local businesses.

cards.title: Downtown Connector
cards.subtitle: Water Street Corridor
cards.notes: Use this street to transition between the university's academic core and the shops of West King Street.
cards.short_summary: A short but vital connector street that links the campus directly to the heart of downtown Boone.
cards.evidence_claim: Water Street is a historical street that connects the university area to the public square and King Street.
cards.access_notes: Public street with sidewalk access; connects to the Jones House Cultural Center.

cards.title: Residential Pocket
cards.subtitle: Faculty Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this quiet street behind the Convocation Center, home to several long-standing student apartment buildings.
cards.short_summary: A residential street tucked behind the university's athletic facilities, primarily serving as a student housing area.
cards.evidence_claim: Faculty Street contains student housing such as Appalachian South and is located near the Holmes Convocation Center.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street with limited street parking.

cards.title: Library and Academic Row
cards.subtitle: College Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Belk Library and Information Commons or the College of Education along this central campus street.
cards.short_summary: A key academic street that houses the university's main library and several major departmental buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: College Street is the location of the Belk Library and Information Commons and the Reich College of Education.
cards.access_notes: Primarily a pedestrian and university service street with restricted vehicle access.

cards.title: Student Activities Row
cards.subtitle: Locust Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here to find the Office of Campus Activities and the Plemmons Student Union entrance.
cards.short_summary: A central street for student life, providing access to the student union and various campus activity offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Locust Street houses the Office of Campus Activities and provides access to the Plemmons Student Union.
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian-heavy street with limited vehicle access near the student union.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From the ringing of the Founders Bell to the high-fives of the Mountaineer Walk, these traditions define the black and gold spirit of Appalachian State University.

cards.title: The Mountaineer Walk
cards.subtitle: A pre-game high-five ritual
cards.notes: Line the path from Trivette Hall to Kidd Brewer Stadium two hours before kickoff to high-five the football team as they head to the locker room.
cards.short_summary: The Mountaineer Walk is a pre-game tradition where fans and the marching band line the sidewalk to cheer on the football team as they arrive at the stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mountaineer Walk occurs before each home game, with fans lining the sidewalk from Trivette Hall to Kidd Brewer Stadium to greet the team.
cards.source_title: Catch the Spirit of Mountaineer Walk Before Each Home Game - App State Athletics
cards.access_notes: Occurs approximately two hours before home football games along the stadium path.

cards.title: Ringing the Founders Bell
cards.subtitle: Marking the start and end of the journey
cards.notes: Visit Founders Plaza to ring the historic bell during orientation to mark your arrival and again at graduation to celebrate your academic success.
cards.short_summary: The Founders Bell, located at Founders Plaza, is rung by students to symbolize the beginning and completion of their academic journey at App State.
cards.evidence_claim: Students are invited to ring the Founders Bell at the beginning of their journey and again following their graduation ceremony.
cards.source_title: Alumni Hall & Ringing the Founders' Bell - App State Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Located at Founders Plaza; accessible during campus events and graduation.

cards.title: The Hi Hi Yikas Fight Song
cards.subtitle: A unique mountain victory chant
cards.notes: Learn the lyrics to the university fight song and join the crowd in singing it whenever the Mountaineers score a touchdown at The Rock.
cards.short_summary: Hi Hi Yikas is the official fight song of Appalachian State University, performed by the Marching Mountaineers and sung by fans during athletic events.
cards.evidence_claim: Hi Hi Yikas is the university's fight song, played when the football team scores or wins.
cards.access_notes: Performed at Kidd Brewer Stadium and other athletic venues during games.

cards.title: The Yosef Statue
cards.subtitle: A symbol of 'Your Self'
cards.notes: Stop by the bronze statue of the Mountaineer mascot, Yosef, whose name is mountain slang for 'yourself,' representing every member of the App State family.
cards.short_summary: The Yosef Statue is a bronze monument of the university's mascot, symbolizing the resilient spirit of the Appalachian people.
cards.evidence_claim: The Yosef statue is a university landmark; the name Yosef is mountain talk for 'yourself.'
cards.source_title: The Mountain Man Statue: The Story Behind App State's "Yosef"
cards.access_notes: Located on campus near the Duck Pond and Sanford Mall; open to the public.

cards.title: The Duck Pond Victory Jump
cards.subtitle: A post-win celebration
cards.notes: Watch as students celebrate major football victories by jumping into the campus Duck Pond, a tradition that surged after the 2022 win over Texas A&M.
cards.short_summary: The Duck Pond Victory Jump is a spontaneous student celebration following significant football wins, where fans leap into the campus pond.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition of jumping into the duck pond began or was revitalized after the win against Texas A&M in 2022.
cards.source_title: OPINION: Ducks don't like drunks - The Appalachian
cards.access_notes: Occurs at the Duck Pond on the corner of River St. and Stadium Dr. after major wins.

cards.title: Rosen Sculpture Walk
cards.subtitle: An annual outdoor art competition
cards.notes: Take a self-guided tour of the ten new contemporary sculptures installed across campus each year as part of this four-decade-old competition.
cards.short_summary: The Rosen Sculpture Walk is an annual competition and exhibition featuring ten outdoor sculptures placed throughout the App State campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Martin and Doris Rosen Outdoor Sculpture Competition features 10 new installations on campus each year.
cards.source_title: Four decades of art are celebrated with the Turchin Center's Rosen Sculpture Walk
cards.access_notes: Sculptures are located outdoors across the campus; accessible year-round.

cards.title: Bell Ringers Society Induction
cards.subtitle: Honoring university history
cards.notes: Attend the Founders Day ceremony to see new members inducted into the Bell Ringers Society, where they ring the bell to honor the school's 1899 founding.
cards.short_summary: The Bell Ringers Society is an honorary group whose members ring the Founders Bell during the annual Founders Day celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bell Ringers Society was established to honor individuals who represent the history of the institution during Founders Day.
cards.source_title: App State celebrates 120 years of education at Founders Day - The Appalachian
cards.access_notes: Induction ceremony held annually on Founders Day (typically in September or October) at Founders Plaza.

cards.title: Yosef's Musket Fire
cards.subtitle: A loud touchdown celebration
cards.notes: Listen for the blast of Yosef's rifle, which is fired into the air after every Mountaineer touchdown at home football games.
cards.short_summary: Yosef's Musket Fire is a tradition where the mascot fires a rifle to celebrate each touchdown scored by the App State football team.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2006 football season saw the return of Yosef's rifle which is fired after every Appalachian touchdown.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during home football games at Kidd Brewer Stadium.

cards.entity_name: Black and Gold Game Day Bibs
cards.title: Black and Gold Game Day Bibs
cards.subtitle: The unofficial student uniform
cards.notes: Don a pair of striped black and gold overalls, a staple of the student section at 'The Rock' since the early 2000s.
cards.short_summary: Game Day Bibs are black and gold striped overalls worn by students and fans as a signature display of school spirit during football games.
cards.evidence_claim: Students and alumni wear game day bibs, often in black and gold vertical stripes, as part of their game day attire.
cards.source_title: Game day at The Rock: A new Mountaineer's guide - The Appalachian
cards.access_notes: Worn by fans at Kidd Brewer Stadium; available for purchase at the campus bookstore.

cards.title: The Tennessee Waltz Post-Game
cards.subtitle: A melodic end to game day
cards.notes: Stay in your seats after the game to hear the Marching Mountaineers perform 'The Tennessee Waltz,' a tradition requested by fans since the 1970s.
cards.short_summary: The Tennessee Waltz is a traditional post-game song performed by the university's marching band after every football game.
cards.evidence_claim: The band's post-game show includes 'The Tennessee Waltz,' which was added as a standard in the 1970s.
cards.source_title: Appalachian State University Marching Mountaineers - Wikipedia
cards.access_notes: Performed at the conclusion of home football games at Kidd Brewer Stadium.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Appalachian State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Fuel Up for Move-In
cards.subtitle: Central Dining Hall
cards.notes: Start your weekend at the main dining hub. Use your meal plan swipes for all-you-care-to-eat options at select stations during the fall opening schedule.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-access dining facility on campus, often referred to as Central Dining Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Street Café (Central Dining Hall) is an all-access dining facility that accepts meal plan swipes and has specific hours during the fall opening period.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours - App State Campus Dining
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday-Sunday 9:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. during regular semesters; check fall opening schedules for specific move-in hours.

cards.title: Gear Up with Black and Gold
cards.subtitle: 219 College Street
cards.notes: Visit the bookstore to pick up your Mountaineer apparel and textbooks. All profits from your purchases go toward academic scholarships for students.
cards.short_summary: The official university bookstore providing textbooks, technology, and licensed Mountaineer merchandise.
cards.evidence_claim: The App State Campus Store is located at 219 College Street and profits support student scholarships.
cards.source_title: Our Stores - App State Campus Store
cards.access_notes: Located between the student union and library; check website for specific weekend move-in hours.

cards.title: Connect at the Campus Core
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Head to this central green space for Welcome Week festivities. It's the primary spot for student organizations to host outdoor meet-and-greets.
cards.short_summary: A large open lawn in the center of campus used for student gatherings, events, and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanford Mall is a central location for Welcome Week events and student engagement activities.
cards.source_title: Welcome to App | Office of Campus Activities
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space accessible 24/7; events typically occur during daylight hours.

cards.title: Snap a Mountaineer Photo
cards.subtitle: Stadium Drive & Rivers Street
cards.notes: Take your first official college photo with the bronze statue of Yosef, the university's mascot, located near the entrance to the stadium area.
cards.short_summary: A prominent bronze statue of the App State mascot, Yosef, serving as a popular campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The Yosef statue is located at the corner of Stadium Drive and Rivers Street and is a popular photo spot.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark accessible 24/7 for photos.

cards.title: Explore Student Life Hub
cards.subtitle: 263 Locust Street
cards.notes: Visit the union to find student organization offices, the solarium, and various dining options like Cascades Café. It's the center for campus involvement.
cards.short_summary: The main student union building housing campus activities, meeting spaces, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Plemmons Student Union is the hub for student life and has specific weekend hours (Saturday 10am-6pm, Sunday 3pm-11pm).
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and Sunday 3:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. during the semester.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: 218 College Street
cards.notes: Walk through the library to locate the 24/5 study areas and the technology checkout desk. It's a great place to set up your laptop before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The main university library offering extensive study spaces, research help, and technology rentals.
cards.evidence_claim: Belk Library is the main library on campus and operates on a 24/5 schedule during the semester.
cards.access_notes: Opens Sunday at 10:00 a.m. and remains open 24 hours until Friday at 9:00 p.m. during regular semesters.

cards.title: Experience Local Art
cards.subtitle: 423 West King Street
cards.notes: Take a break from move-in to browse contemporary art galleries. Admission is always free, and it's located right where campus meets downtown Boone.
cards.short_summary: The university's visual arts center featuring multiple galleries of contemporary art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Turchin Center for the Visual Arts offers free admission and is open on Saturdays from 10 am to 6 pm.
cards.source_title: Visit | Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Thursday and Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Friday 12:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

cards.title: Relax at Tomlinson Park
cards.subtitle: Rivers Street
cards.notes: Enjoy a quiet moment by the water at the campus duck pond. It's a classic spot for students to unwind and watch the resident ducks.
cards.short_summary: A scenic pond and park area on campus popular for relaxation and nature watching.
cards.evidence_claim: Tomlinson Park/Duck Pond is a recognized campus landmark located on Rivers Street.
cards.source_title: Tomlinson Park / Duck Pond at App State - Campus Maps
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park area accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Check Out the Gym
cards.subtitle: 150 Bodenheimer Drive
cards.notes: Visit the SRC to see the climbing wall, pool, and fitness floors. Bring your AppCard to gain entry and start your fitness routine early.
cards.short_summary: The primary indoor recreation facility for students, featuring fitness equipment, courts, and a pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Recreation Center (SRC) is the main campus gym and requires an AppCard for student access.
cards.access_notes: Check the UREC website or app for specific weekend hours during Welcome Week.

cards.title: Stroll Through Downtown Boone
cards.subtitle: Main Street of Boone
cards.notes: End your first weekend with a walk down King Street. Explore local shops and restaurants that define the unique culture of the High Country.
cards.short_summary: The main thoroughfare of downtown Boone, bordering the university and filled with local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: King Street is the primary commercial street in downtown Boone and is adjacent to the App State campus.
cards.access_notes: Public street; individual business hours vary, but many shops are open on weekends.
